correctness.rationale: The independent-Poisson representation yields the exact Bernoulli variance sum. For 0<beta<1, a transition-window Riemann sum gives V_beta(t)~(log 2/beta)(log(t/Z_beta))^(1/beta-1), which diverges; the Lyapunov ratio is bounded by V_beta(t)^(-1/2). At beta=1, the centered count converges along phase subsequences to a well-defined integer-valued Bernoulli series. At beta>1, the explicit sequence t_m=Z_beta exp((m+gamma/(beta m^(beta-1)))^beta) leaves only urn m random in the limit, giving a nondegenerate Bernoulli law. These analytic arguments prove the claimed iff statement; no finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The stretched-exponential family is a natural one-parameter model for ultra-light-tailed urn frequencies. The transition width grows, stays bounded, or shrinks as beta crosses 1; the theorem identifies the corresponding Gaussian, phase-indexed discrete, and single-Bernoulli regimes and gives the exact variance scale. This supplies a concrete boundary for when Gaussian occupancy approximations are valid.
